physicalNotes: Radius 1.878 Jupiter radii from Simonnin et al. 2025 (2025A&A...698A.314S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...698A.314S/abstract): 134,262 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 1.83 Jupiter masses (Simonnin et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025A&A...698A.314S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...698A.314S/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Simonnin et al. 2025 (2025A&A...698A.314S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SIMONNIN_ET_AL_2025): P 1.90261131 d
sources.shape: Simonnin et al. 2025 (2025A&A...698A.314S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SIMONNIN_ET_AL_2025): a/R* 4.109; Simonnin et al. 2025 (2025A&A...698A.314S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SIMONNIN_ET_AL_2025): inclination 77.626 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Simonnin et al. 2025 (2025A&A...698A.314S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SIMONNIN_ET_AL_2025): transit mid-time 2459983.791942 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
